title: OpenCloud repeats the Nextcloud gap: file events but no record of business decisions
content:
OpenCloud is described as the newer German sovereign file platform, and the research places it in the same shape as Nextcloud: the system produces file events and nothing about the business decisions those files are evidence of.

The gap is a category difference rather than a missing feature. A file event says a document changed; it does not say that a request was approved, a claim rejected, or an obligation accepted. Sovereign file storage answers where the artefact lives and under whose jurisdiction it sits — it does not answer who decided what, which is the object public-sector audit asks about.

Timing is what separates this lead from the Nextcloud leads elsewhere in the corpus. Heinlein backs OpenCloud and the platform is new, so the record layer can be designed into it rather than retrofitted around an established interface. Early is cheaper on both sides: fewer compatibility constraints, and a say in where the events are emitted from.
